extraction.name: MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI
extraction.description: MMMU is a benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.citeAs: Xiang Yue et al., MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI, arXiv:2311.16502, 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark collection takes three stages. First, common university majors were reviewed to select subjects where visual inputs are commonly adopted. Second, over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in these majors were recruited as annotators to assist in question collection. They collected multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary. The annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations. To avoid data contamination, annotators were advised to select questions without immediately available answers. The process resulted in a diverse collection of 13K questions. Data quality control involved two steps: identifying potential duplicates via lexical overlap and source URL similarity, and distributing problems among co-authors for format and typo checking. Finally, problems were categorized into difficulty levels, and approximately 10% classified as 'very easy' were excluded.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: College exams, quizzes, and textbooks from six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering. Sources include online resources, textbooks, and lecture materials.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Data quality control involved identifying potential duplicates using lexical overlap and source URL similarity, which were then reviewed and eliminated. Problems were distributed among co-authors for format and typo checking. Problems were categorized into four difficulty levels (very easy, easy, medium, hard), and approximately 10% classified as 'very easy' were excluded.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Suspected duplicates were reviewed and eliminated. Co-authors checked for format and typos. Problems were categorized by difficulty, and 'very easy' problems were excluded. Questions were formatted into JSON files with specific naming conventions for questions and images.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, were recruited as annotators. They collected questions from textbooks and online resources. Annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright regulations and avoid data from sites prohibiting copy/redistribution. They were advised to select questions without immediately available answers to prevent data contamination. Annotations included question text, answer options, correct answer, image types, question difficulty, and explanations. A secondary review team vetted annotations for quality and guideline adherence. Regular audits were conducted.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Error analysis was performed on 150 randomly sampled error instances from GPT-4V. Errors were categorized into Perceptual Errors (35%), Lack of Knowledge (29%), Reasoning Errors (26%), Textual Understanding Errors (4%), Rejection to Answer (3%), Annotation Errors (2%), and Answer Extraction Errors (1%).
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the respective majors/subjects.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is available at https://mmmu-benchmark.github.io/. A live-updating leaderboard is available. Version history includes V1 (Nov 27), V2 (Dec 18), V3 (Dec 21), and V4 (June 13).
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: MMMU aims to stimulate the community to build next-generation multimodal foundation models towards expert artificial general intelligence. It highlights the challenges posed by expert-level tasks and the gap between current models and human experts. The benchmark is intended to monitor progress towards Expert AGI, which is associated with risks of job displacement and economic disruption.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases. The focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI. The dataset covers 30 subjects and 183 subfields, but some subjects like law and linguistics were ruled out because it was difficult to find enough relevant multimodal problems.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI as defined by Morris et al., because there lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and the '90th percentile of skilled adults,' nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI shall tackle. The manual curation process may carry biases. The focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. The benchmark is designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It is used to assess expert-level multimodal understanding capability of foundation models.
